chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir from 'Uthman ibn Yazid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever performs the ritual bath (ghusl) after the dawn breaks, that bath suffices him until the night, in every place where the bath is obligatory; and whoever performs the ritual bath at night, that bath suffices him until the dawn breaks."

key_terms.طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ: Dawn break (rising of the morning light)
key_terms.يَجِبُ فِيهِ الْغُسْلُ: Where the bath is obligatory (referring to places/conditions requiring ghusl)

ai.seo_question: How long does a ritual bath (ghusl) remain valid if performed outside of its specific obligatory time?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in the chapter on the state of Ihram within *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, clarifies the temporal validity of the major ritual bath (ghusl) when performed outside its specific obligatory triggers, such as Janabah or Hayd. It establishes a legal principle where bathing after dawn suffices until nightfall, and night bathing suffices until the next dawn, providing flexibility for pilgrims and believers in maintaining ritual purity. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the interplay between specific obligatory baths and general purification requirements.
